mainEntity.name: When should I hire a general contractor instead of individual subcontractors?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need a general contractor when a project involves multiple trades, structural alterations, or required building permits. Simple single-trade tasks, like replacing a standard water heater or painting a room, can usually be handled directly by specialized subcontractors or handy services. However, whole-home additions, commercial build-outs, and major kitchen or bathroom remodels require coordinating electricians, plumbers, framers, and dry-wallers. A general contractor oversees the entire schedule, secures necessary municipal permits, manages safety on-site, and ensures work meets building codes. Hiring a general contractor removes the burden of managing conflicting subcontractor schedules and resolves quality issues through a single point of accountability.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hire a general contractor for projects involving multiple trades, structural changes, or building permits. Single-trade updates can often be handled directly by specialized trades.
